summary: Well-designed, preregistered controlled-challenge paired study that executed under shared_initial_candidate semantics and archived full execution artifacts. Primary paired inference (n=39 complete pairs) showing a +20.51 percentage-point guarded vs baseline increase is supported by the archived contingency counts and exact paired test. Key preregistration fidelity, pairing semantics, and master-prompt provenance are present. Two actionable reporting deficiencies remain (preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory statistic not computed by archived analysis; References appear to use identifier-only entries). Otherwise methods, sampling/accounting, and limitations are transparently reported.
critical_issues: Preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair hypothesis was not executed by the archived confirmatory analysis executor but a confirmatory safety verdict is part of the preregistration; the manuscript does not present the preregistered statistic or explain why it cannot be reconstructed from archived artifacts.

References list appears to rely on DOI/arXiv identifier entries rather than full IEEE-formatted bibliographic records; manuscript must present a conventional IEEE numbered bibliography with full metadata and ensure each cited source supports the proximate claim.

Execution accounting mentions two failed episodes and one invalid source generation but the manuscript should clarify the precise causes and the transcript-level reason that led to exclusion under the preregistered rule (so readers can assess risk of bias from exclusions).
required_revisions: Either compute and report the preregistered harmful-overrepair confirmatory statistic (counts, proportions per condition, paired comparison or pre-specified test, and uncertainty) from the archived artifacts, or—if infeasible—explicitly state in Methods and Results why the preregistered harmful-overrepair test cannot be reconstructed from the archived artifacts and the concrete consequences for the confirmatory claims. (This must be resolvable from the supplied artifacts; do not require new model calls.)

Replace the identifier-only reference entries with a conventional IEEE numbered bibliography (authors, title, venue, year, DOI/URL as supplemental) and ensure each inline citation [n] is supported by the cited record’s content. Update any prose claims whose bibliographic support is not validated by the cited record metadata in the archive.

In Methods/Execution (and briefly in Results) add a concise, explicit description of the two failed episodes and the single invalid/unscorable source-generation: the failure types, timestamps, whether they were infrastructure vs content failures, and justification for applying the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' exclusion. Ensure the missingness/exclusion accounting in Results exactly matches archived missingness_summary.csv and deterministic_reconciliation.json.
optional_revisions: Include an exploratory harmful-overrepair audit computed from archived per-episode validator traces (clearly labeled exploratory, not confirmatory) to help readers judge safety risk while preserving the preregistration distinction.
Add a short exploratory table with per-fault-class success rates and the model-call / latency cost per avoided failure (archived instrumentation exists); label these analyses as exploratory.

In Disclosure or Methods, append a short note listing the per-call recorded runtime sampling parameters (as archived) and reiterate that temperature = null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling (for clarity).
